setup.title: Add a field
setup.locationHelp: Stand in or near the field and tap the button. This is used for the weather.
setup.locationDeniedBody: Without it we will use a default location for the weather forecast. You can change this later.
setup.locationFailedBody: Check that location is switched on and try again.
setup.s1Body: Find the Drikr sensor box and switch it on. Wait about half a minute for its light to come on steadily.
setup.s2Title: Has this box been set up before?
setup.s2Body: A brand new box has no WiFi saved. You tell it your WiFi name and password once, from your phone, and it remembers.
setup.s2First: Set it up for the first time
setup.s3Body: The box makes its own temporary WiFi so your phone can reach it. Join that, pick your home WiFi from the list, and the box restarts on your network.
setup.s3Step2: Join the network called Drikr_Setup - the password is on the sticker on the box
setup.s3Step3: A setup page should open by itself. Pick your WiFi from the list, type the password, and save.
setup.s3Hint: Your phone will warn that Drikr_Setup has no internet - that is normal, it is just the box. If no page opens, tap "Open the setup page" below.
setup.s4Body: Make sure your phone is back on your normal WiFi, then search. This usually takes a few seconds.
setup.notFound: Could not find the box. Check it is switched on and that your phone is on the same WiFi, then try again or type its address below.
setup.addressHint: Shown on the box, or in its setup page. You can type a name like drikr.local or a number like 192.168.1.50.
setup.s5Body: Found {{count}} sensor(s) in the field. Choose which field they are in.
setup.s5NoNodes: The box is working but cannot hear any field sensors yet. Check they are switched on and within about a kilometre.
setup.whichField: Which field are these sensors in?
setup.s6Body: If you have a moisture or pH probe plugged in, record two readings so the app knows what its numbers mean.
setup.probeNotFitted: Not set up - readings will show as no sensor
setup.s6SkipNote: No probe plugged in? Skip this. Those readings will simply show as no sensor, which is correct.
setup.calLowHint: Hold the probe in dry air, away from soil and water. Enter the number the app shows.
setup.calHighHint: Now put the probe in a glass of water. Enter the number again.
setup.calBothNeeded: Both readings are needed, and they must be different - otherwise there is no way to tell wet from dry.
setup.s7Body: Your field data will update every few minutes. The sensors sleep in between to save their batteries, so a reading a few minutes old is normal.
setup.helpQ1: I can't find the Drikr_Setup WiFi
setup.helpA1: Hold the button on the box for five seconds to restart setup mode, then look again. If it still does not appear, switch the box off and on.
setup.helpQ2: I set up the WiFi but the app cannot find the box
setup.helpA2: Check your phone is on your home WiFi and not on mobile data. Also check you typed the WiFi password correctly - if the box could not join, it goes back to making its own Drikr_Setup network.
setup.helpQ3: The box is found but shows no sensors
setup.helpA3: The field sensors are separate battery units. Check they are switched on, and that they are within about a kilometre of the box with nothing large in between.
setup.helpA4: That is normal and correct. It means that sensor is not fitted there. The app shows nothing rather than guessing a number.
setup.helpQ5: Readings are a few minutes old
setup.helpA5: Also normal. The field sensors sleep between readings so their batteries last months instead of days. The app always shows how old a reading is.
setup.resetWifiBody: Hold the BOOT button on the box for 3 seconds while switching it on. It will go back to setup mode so you can choose a different network.
setup.cropSearch: Search your crop (English or local name)
setup.cropNotFound: We do not have advice for "{{query}}" yet. Pick a crop from the list only if it really is what you grow.
setup.monitoring: Do you have Drikr sensors in this field?
setup.modeScoutBody: You check the field with the drone and with photos. The app tells you when to look.
setup.modeSensorBody: The sensors watch the field all the time and warn you.
setup.nameHelp: A name you will recognise, like "North field".
setup.orExactDays: Or type the number of days
setup.stageNow: The crop is now at this stage: {{stage}}. The advice changes as the crop grows.

blast.lookFor: Spindle-shaped grey lesions with dark brown borders, often ringed by a yellow halo
blast.alsoNeeds: Excess nitrogen, and collateral host grasses on the bunds

bacterial_leaf_blight.lookFor: Yellow to straw-white streaks along the leaf edges, spreading down from the tip
bacterial_leaf_blight.alsoNeeds: Strong wind that wounds the leaves, too much fertiliser, deep standing water, and infected stubble nearby

sheath_blight.lookFor: Oval water-soaked patches on the sheath, near the water line

yellow_rust.lookFor: Yellow-orange powdery stripes running in rows along the leaf
yellow_rust.alsoNeeds: Most damaging early in the crop. Yellow leaves are not always rust - confirm before spraying.

powdery_mildew.lookFor: White powdery patches on the upper side of the leaf

karnal_bunt.lookFor: Blackened grain inside the ear with a rotten-fish smell
karnal_bunt.alsoNeeds: Infects at flowering. In north India the protective spray is usually given in mid-February.

downy_mildew.lookFor: Chlorotic streaks with white fungal growth on both leaf surfaces; plants stunted and bushy
downy_mildew.alsoNeeds: Young plants are the most susceptible

turcicum_leaf_blight.lookFor: Long cigar-shaped grey-green lesions, on the lower leaves first
turcicum_leaf_blight.alsoNeeds: Infection starts early in the wet season

common_rust.lookFor: Small cinnamon-brown pustules on both sides of the leaf

root_rot.lookFor: Sudden wilting in patches; bark peels off the root easily
root_rot.alsoNeeds: Dry weather after heavy rain, hot soil, and root damage by grubs or nematodes

bacterial_blight.lookFor: Angular dark-brown spots bounded by the leaf veins

alternaria_leaf_spot.lookFor: Brown spots with concentric rings and grey centres

leaf_curl_virus.lookFor: Leaves curling upward and puckered, plant stunted
leaf_curl_virus.alsoNeeds: Whitefly numbers matter far more than the weather. Check the underside of young leaves for whitefly.

early_blight.lookFor: Dark spots with target-like rings, on the lowest leaves first
early_blight.alsoNeeds: Crop debris left from the previous season

late_blight.lookFor: Water-soaked grey-green patches with white mould on the underside

smut.lookFor: A long black whip growing out of the top of the cane
smut.alsoNeeds: Growing cane year after year, repeated ratoons, and dry weather while the crop tillers

red_rot.lookFor: Split a cane: red inside with white crossbands, smells of alcohol
red_rot.alsoNeeds: Growing cane year after year, repeated ratoons, waterlogging and insect damage

wilt.lookFor: Cane drying from the top down, hollow and light when tapped
wilt.alsoNeeds: Water stress or waterlogging, root damage, and wilt in the previous crop

collar_rot.lookFor: Seedlings collapsing at soil level, black fungal growth on the collar
collar_rot.alsoNeeds: A prolonged rainy spell at the seedling stage, and low-lying ground

tikka_leaf_spot.lookFor: Circular reddish-brown to dark brown spots ringed by a bright yellow halo
tikka_leaf_spot.alsoNeeds: Three days or more of high humidity, heavy nitrogen and phosphorus, and magnesium-deficient soil

rust.lookFor: Orange pustules on the underside of the leaflets

yellow_mosaic_virus.lookFor: Bright yellow patches mixed with green on the leaves
yellow_mosaic_virus.alsoNeeds: Spread by whitefly. Check the underside of young leaves for whitefly.

rust.lookFor: Tiny tan to reddish-brown pustules on the underside of the leaves

charcoal_rot.lookFor: Plants wilt and dry early; grey-black specks inside the lower stem
charcoal_rot.alsoNeeds: A hot dry spell and water stress while the pods fill

wilt.lookFor: Leaves droop and yellow from the bottom up; split the stem and look for brown streaks inside
wilt.alsoNeeds: Warm soil, and wilt in earlier chickpea crops in the same field

ascochyta_blight.lookFor: Brown spots with dark rings on the leaves, stems and pods

dry_root_rot.lookFor: Plants dry up suddenly; the root is black, brittle and has lost its side roots
dry_root_rot.alsoNeeds: Dry, hot soil at flowering and podding

phytophthora_blight.lookFor: Water-soaked patches on the stem near the soil; the stem breaks and the plant dies
phytophthora_blight.alsoNeeds: Waterlogged, low-lying patches after heavy rain

sterility_mosaic.lookFor: Small, pale, crowded leaves with a mosaic pattern; bushy plants with no flowers
sterility_mosaic.alsoNeeds: Spread by tiny mites; old or ratoon pigeon pea plants nearby

wilt.lookFor: Plants wilt in patches; a purple band at the stem base and brown streaks inside
wilt.alsoNeeds: Wilt in earlier pigeon pea crops in the same field

yellow_mosaic_virus.lookFor: Bright yellow patches mixed with green on the leaves
yellow_mosaic_virus.alsoNeeds: Spread by whitefly. Check the underside of young leaves for whitefly.

cercospora_leaf_spot.lookFor: Small brown spots with grey centres and reddish edges on the leaves

powdery_mildew.lookFor: White powdery patches on the leaves

white_rust.lookFor: Raised white blisters on the underside of the leaves; swollen, twisted flower stalks

alternaria_blight.lookFor: Round dark-brown spots with rings on the leaves and pods

stemphylium_blight.lookFor: Yellow-brown streaks on one side of the leaf; the leaf tips dry out

purple_blotch.lookFor: Small white sunken spots that grow into purple patches with yellow edges

late_blight.lookFor: Water-soaked grey-green patches with white mould on the underside
late_blight.alsoNeeds: Cool, foggy or drizzly days one after another. Spreads very fast - act the same day.

early_blight.lookFor: Dark spots with target-like rings, on the oldest leaves first

leaf_curl_virus.lookFor: Leaves curl, crinkle and stay small; the plant is stunted
leaf_curl_virus.alsoNeeds: Spread by whitefly; thrips and mites cause similar curling. Check the underside of young leaves.

anthracnose.lookFor: Sunken dark spots with rings on ripe fruit; shoot tips dying back

bunchy_top.lookFor: Narrow, stiff leaves bunched at the top; dark green dashes along the leaf veins
bunchy_top.alsoNeeds: Spread by the banana aphid and by infected suckers. Remove sick plants with their suckers.

sigatoka_leaf_spot.lookFor: Yellow streaks on the leaves that turn into brown spots with grey centres

downy_mildew.lookFor: Yellow streaks on leaves with white down underneath; ears turn into leafy green heads

ergot.lookFor: Sticky pink or honey-like drops oozing from the ears
ergot.alsoNeeds: Cloudy, drizzly weather while the crop is flowering

blast.lookFor: Spindle-shaped grey spots on the leaves; the neck of the ear turns black and breaks

soil.title: Soil Health Card
soil.lead: Type in the numbers from your Soil Health Card. The app will tell you how much urea, DAP and potash this field needs.
soil.findCard: Lost your card? Find it online
soil.needNpk: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are needed. The rest is optional.
soil.acidic: Your soil is acidic. Ask about adding lime; it lets the crop use the fertiliser better.
soil.alkaline: Your soil is alkaline. Ask about gypsum and add compost; zinc and iron may be short.
soil.salty: Your soil is salty. Water well before sowing and avoid salty water for irrigation.
soil.lowOc: Organic carbon is low. Add 2 tonnes of compost or farmyard manure per acre every season.
soil.planNote: This gives {{n}} kg nitrogen, {{p}} kg phosphate and {{k}} kg potash per hectare, adjusted for your soil.
soil.split: Put all the DAP and potash at sowing. Split the urea: half at sowing, half 3-4 weeks later.
soil.disclaimer: General recommendation. If your card prints its own fertiliser advice for this crop, follow that.

A spraying drone must be type-certified by DGCA and flown by a certified pilot. Farmer groups and hiring centres can get a government subsidy to buy an agricultural drone - ask your agriculture office.

privacy.title: Privacy and your data
privacy.rowSub: What we keep, get a copy, delete everything
privacy.what: Your mobile number, a scrambled form of your PIN, your name and district if you give them, your fields (crop, area, location), sensor readings, warnings, drone flights and photos, and what you post in the community.
privacy.why: Only to give you advice for your field, to keep your fields when you change phones, and to make the community and drone booking work. We never sell your data and show no advertising.
privacy.where: On your phone, and on Google Firebase servers when you are online. Drone photos stay on your phone unless you agree to share them for the crop AI; then they are kept in Drikr's cloud storage (Vercel).
privacy.share: Community posts show your name and district - never your number. In drone booking, your number goes only to the operator who accepts your job. Questions to Kisan Mitra may be sent to Google Gemini to answer. If you tap Translate on a post, its text goes to Bhashini, the Government of India's translation service.
privacy.keep: Until you delete it. Sensor readings are kept by field, without your name or number.
privacy.rights: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you can get a copy of your data, correct it, and have it deleted - with the buttons below. You can also withdraw your consent at any time by deleting your data.
privacy.export: Get a copy of my data
privacy.deleteNote: This removes your account, fields, warnings, posts and bookings from this phone and from our servers. It cannot be undone.
privacy.deleteBody: Your account, fields, warnings, posts and bookings will be removed from this phone and our servers. This cannot be undone.
privacy.deletedLocalOnly: Deleted from this phone. Some data could not be removed from the server - connect to the internet and do this again.
privacy.appIdHelp: Only needed if the Drikr team is making you an expert moderator: send them this ID.

welcome.chooseHint: Tap your language. You will hear it.

setup2.fieldBody: Tell us your crop and mark your field on the map. It takes two minutes.
setup2.sensorsBody: Drikr gives you sensors for free and our team installs them. They watch your soil and weather all day.
setup2.smsBody: Add one family member's number. When an urgent alert comes, one tap sends it to them by SMS, even to a basic phone.
setup2.photosBody: May we use your drone photos to train Drikr's crop AI? Only the photos and where they were taken are sent. You can change this any time in Privacy.
setup2.voiceBody: Tap the green mic at the bottom of any screen and speak. Try: "How is my field?", "Weather", or "Read my alerts". Hold the mic to hear help for that screen.

kit.what: Drikr gives the kit and our team comes to install it. In the kit:

kit.item2: A base station at the edge of your field (no SIM, no bill)
kit.item3: Installation and setup by our team
kit.addFieldFirst: Add your field first, so our team knows where to come. You can still ask now.

kit.failed: Could not send. Check your internet and try again.

assistant.noField: You have not added a field yet. Say "add field".
assistant.allGood: {{name}}. No problems right now. Keep going as usual.
assistant.helpGeneral: Tap the mic and say what you want.
assistant.examples: You can say: how is my field, read my alerts, weather, mandi price, fly the drone, free sensors, call helpline, go back.

guide.Login: Type your mobile number and tap Next. Then make a 4 digit PIN you will remember.
guide.HomeTab: This is Home. The top card tells you how your field is and what to do today. The big buttons open the map, photo check, drone and questions.
guide.FieldsTab: These are your fields. Tap a field to see it, or tap plus to add another.
guide.AlertsTab: These are your alerts. The most urgent is at the top. Tap one to see what to do.
guide.ProfileTab: Here you change language, alerts, family SMS numbers and read aloud.
guide.FieldHealthMap: This is your field map. Green is healthy, yellow needs a look, red is the problem area. Tap a square to learn more.
guide.Drone: Here the drone checks your field. Join the drone's WiFi, then tap the big button. It flies, takes photos and lands by itself.
guide.Weather: This is the weather for the next days, and the best time to spray.
guide.Market: These are today's mandi prices, and the best mandi near you after transport cost.
guide.Community: Here farmers share what worked. Type at the bottom to post. Never share your phone number.
guide.Schemes: Here is government help: PM-KISAN, crop insurance, MSP prices and free helplines.
guide.SoilCard: Type the numbers from your Soil Health Card. You will get how many bags of fertiliser to use.
guide.Claim: Make a crop insurance report here. Choose what caused the loss, add photos, and make the PDF. Report within 72 hours.
guide.DroneBooking: Ask for a drone for your field here. Choose spray or check, your district and the area.
guide.Scout: Take a clear photo of one leaf. Then tell us what you see.
guide.KisanMitra: Ask any farming question, by typing or with the mic. The answer is read aloud.
guide.SensorNodes: These are your sensors and their latest readings.
guide.SensorKit: Drikr gives you sensors for free. Tap Get free sensors and our team will call you.
guide.AlertDetail: This alert tells you what is wrong, where, and what to do. Tell us if it was right.
guide.FieldSetup: Choose your crop, then your sowing date, then mark your field. Tap Next after each step.
guide.RiskDetail: This explains one risk to your crop, and what is causing it.
guide.Privacy: Here you see what Drikr keeps, and you can download or delete your data.
